title: Quick start
intro: Start with one assignment: prepare the questions, check student answers, grade and review, then view the results.

sections.title: What you need for your first assignment
sections.body:
• Sign in with your teacher account and check which models are enabled in Models & BYOK.
  • Prepare the questions. You can also supply reference answers, grading criteria and programming test cases.
  • Collect one submission per student. For programming assignments, collect one self-contained source file per student. Handwritten Python is also supported. You can upload the class set as one ZIP. Prepare a list of student IDs if you want to match by roster.

Upload formats at a glance · roster example

sections.title: Complete a grading cycle
sections.body:
1. In “New task,” enter a name and semester, with an optional course and tags.
  2. Upload questions, set the maximum score for each question, and click “Recognize and prepare question materials.”
  3. In “Question Material Overview,” check the question text, maximum scores, grading criteria, and reference answers.
  4. Upload student submissions and check student identities and the content for each question.
  5. Select grading models and a scoring method, select “Save & Review Grading,” and check the summary.
  6. After grading finishes, resolve red items first, then open “Performance Analysis & Exports.”

Once the grading summary passes its checks, a countdown starts and grading begins automatically. To change settings, click “Back to grading settings” before the countdown ends.

sections.title: Remember the two colors
sections.body:
• Red · Action required. Open the item, correct the missing or invalid information, and save. If the page asks for confirmation, check the original or grading evidence first.
  • Yellow · Suggested review. You can continue or check the item first. For example, low confidence means the model was less certain about this particular judgment.

sections.title: Upload formats at a glance
sections.body:
Documents include PDF, text-based Word (.docx), TXT and Markdown (.md, .markdown).
Still images include JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, TIF and TIFF.

Upload toAccepted input
QuestionsDocuments or images
Reference answersDocuments or images
Grading criteriaDocuments, images or typed criteria
Programming test casesDocuments, images, JSON or CSV
Written submissionsDocuments or still images. Upload an individual file or a class archive, up to 100 MiB.
Programming submissionsOne source file per student (.py, .c, .cc or .cpp). Handwritten Python can be submitted as an image or scanned PDF. Upload a single submission or a class archive.
Student rosterCSV, TSV or TXT. Student ID is required; name is optional.
Course libraryDocuments up to 64 MiB each or images up to 10 MiB each.
Task knowledge filesSame formats and size limits as the course library. Up to 20 files per task.
Materials for existing questionsChoose one source at a time. Select “Test cases” to use JSON or CSV.

When setting up questions, supply the questions and optionally add reference answers, grading criteria or test cases. Choose up to one source per category. Each new file can be up to 5 MiB, with up to 400,000 characters of extracted text.

details.title: Image dimensions and Word content
details.body: Use images up to 8,192 pixels on the longest side and 16 million pixels in total. Use single-page TIFFs. Text-based Word files preserve ordinary paragraphs, tables, spaces, tabs and line breaks. If a question relies on equation objects, embedded figures or tracked changes, upload a PDF that preserves them.

details.title: When a Word document exceeds the reading limit
details.body: A DOCX can contain up to 500 parts, up to 5 MiB per part and 100 MiB total when unpacked. Its text limit is 500,000 characters, or 400,000 for question materials.

title: Registration and sign-in
intro: Create a teacher account with your school email, or continue with an existing account.

sections.title: Create a teacher account
sections.body:
1. On the home page, select “Register / Sign in,” then “Register with email verification” below the sign-in form.
  2. Enter a username, school email, password, and password confirmation.
  3. Click “Send verification link,” open the email, and complete verification.
  4. After verification, return to the sign-in page and open the workspace.

Usernames must contain at least 3 characters; passwords must contain 8–128 characters. The link is valid for 30 minutes. Verifying your email creates your account.

details.title: Verification email not received
details.body: Check your spam folder first. On the email notification page, resend after the countdown finishes. If your email domain is not accepted, check your school email against the instructions on the page.

sections.title: Sign in and reset your password
sections.body:
On the sign-in page, choose “Username” or “Email,” enter the corresponding username or email address and your password, then select “Sign in.”

To reset your password, select “Forgot password” below the password field and follow the link sent to your email.

To sign out, open your username menu at the top right. If your session expires, sign in again and reopen the assignment from History.

title: Workspace and task history
intro: The Workspace shows tasks that need your attention. To find a previous assignment, open History and choose Grading. Textbook recognition and Saved drafts each have their own tab.

sections.title: Resume tasks from the workspace
sections.body:
In the Workspace, find your assignment under “Tasks requiring attention” and check its current stage. Select the link under “Next step” to continue where you left off.

During recognition or grading, open the progress page for updates. “Estimating” means the remaining time is being calculated.

sections.title: Find grading tasks with Ask SmarTAI
sections.body:
Find the Ask SmarTAI search box below the cards in the Workspace, or on the Grading tab in History.

Enter a task name, course, tag or question, then select “Ask SmarTAI.”

  • Which Fall 2026 calculus assignments need review?
  • With a passing score of 60%, which assignments had a pass rate below 80%?

To clear the current filters, select × at the right of the search box.

sections.title: Edit or delete a task
sections.body:
To edit the name, semester, course or tags, open the task and select “New Task,” step 1 in the task’s progress bar. Make your changes and select “Save & Return.” If another page has updated the task, check the latest details before saving.

To delete a task, select the trash icon beside it in the task list. Check the name and what will be deleted in the dialog. Choose “Confirm deletion” to proceed or “Cancel” to keep the task.

title: Models & BYOK
intro: BYOK means using your own model API configuration. Configure it once, then select it for different tasks and stages.

sections.title: Add and enable a model
sections.body:
1. Open the username menu in the upper-right corner → “Models & BYOK” → “Add configuration.”
  2. Select a provider and enter the model name and API key. The configuration name is optional.
  3. Normally, keep the default API Base URL. For a relay service, use the URL and model ID from the relay provider’s documentation.
  4. Save and enable the configuration, then select the model on the task page.

Once saved and enabled, the model is available in your tasks. To try it first, use one of the optional tests below.

details.title: Base URL, protocol, and RPM
details.body: Copy the provider’s base URL, including any prefix such as /v1. For an official API, choose “Follow provider.” For a relay, use its documented protocol. RPM means requests per minute. Leave it blank or enter 0 for automatic pacing.

sections.title: Test and manage configurations
sections.body:
“Verify (optional)” tests text connectivity; “Verify vision capability” tests image input. Requests are sent only after you confirm the test prompt, and tests may consume provider quota.

  • If you see “Could not confirm this time,” open the reason and check the model name and image permissions before retrying.
  • When editing a configuration, leave API key blank to retain the existing key.
  • You can set a default, enable, disable, or delete configurations. Choose another default before disabling or deleting the current default model.
  • You can use different models for question recognition, submission recognition, and grading.

You can select an enabled model in a task. To check your balance and usage, open “Usage” under the provider links at the bottom of the page.

sections.title: Choosing and using LLM and OCR services
sections.body:
Large language models and OCR services serve different purposes: LLMs interpret questions, generate reference materials, and grade assignments. Image-capable LLMs can also recognize images, scans, and handwritten answers. OCR services extract text and structure from documents; grading after recognition still requires a grading model. Choose based on file type, recognition quality, and service quota, and check the recognized results.

For an LLM API, enter the provider, model name, API Key, and API base address in “Add model configuration.” For OCR, use the credential configuration area for that service. For example, Baidu document parsing has a separate API Key / Secret Key configuration area; credentials can be validated after saving. Service permissions and quotas are checked during actual OCR tasks.

Provider links cover Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Zhipu, Kimi, Qwen, Tencent TokenHub, Doubao, MiniMax, and Baidu OCR. Find the provider at the bottom of the page, click “Keys” to apply in its official console, then return to the relevant configuration area. Check model names under the provider’s “Documentation”; check free quota, balances, and billing under “Usage.” For relay services, use the Key, Base URL, and model ID supplied by the relay provider, and contact that provider first if there are problems.

Need field-by-field instructions or help applying for a key? See Model configuration steps, Application guides for 11 providers, or School and other relay APIs.

title: Course library
intro: Keep reusable textbooks, lecture notes, answers, and grading criteria together so you can select them directly next time.

sections.title: Upload and categorize materials
sections.body:
1. Open the course library, select “Upload” and choose one document (up to 64 MiB) or still image (up to 10 MiB). See Upload formats at a glance.
  2. If useful, choose a course, group or material type and add tags. Select “Upload.”
  3. Once parsing finishes, search the text or attach the material to a task.

details.title: Reading text, images and scanned pages
details.body: For text-based Word files, TXT, Markdown and PDFs with a text layer, you can select “Existing text only (no model calls).” Choose a vision or OCR model for images or scanned pages. Background recognition may incur model charges.

sections.title: Find, reference, and manage materials
sections.body:
Use the search at the top to find filenames, tags, or groups, and filter by type. When uploading questions, you can select sources from the library. In grading settings, you can also select textbooks, lecture notes, and other supplementary context.

Material management lets you change names, courses, groups, and tags without rewriting parsed text. Check task-reference warnings before deleting. Deleting materials also removes their reference associations.

sections.title: When parsing is incomplete
sections.body:
Open the file’s recognition status to see which pages still need attention and why. Choose a model to retry those pages. Pages that were read successfully are kept.

The course library uses separate storage. Saved library content is retained long-term and is not deleted with grading tasks. Space from deleted materials is reclaimed in the background.

sections.title: Find a passage inside a file
sections.body:
Use the search box at the top of the Course library to find a file. To find a passage inside files, narrow the list to 20 files or fewer. Enter a keyword or question under “Search material content” and select the magnifying glass. Open a source reference in the results to see the passage in context.

“Local search” is the default. “Model-assisted” search sends only your query to a model and may incur a charge. Local results remain available if the assisted search fails. The same search is available in the task materials area of grading settings.

title: New tasks and drafts
intro: Give the assignment a clear name, then prepare the questions.

sections.title: Enter task information
sections.body:
Choose “New Task” in the top navigation, name the assignment and select a semester. To add an optional course or tag, type its name and select a match or create a new one.

For example, name the task “Calculus · Chapter 3 Assignment,” choose the course “Calculus” and add the tag “Chapter 3.” Select “Create & Add Questions” to open the upload page.

sections.title: Save drafts, restore work, and save to the task
sections.body:
When leaving an editor, choose the draft option to keep your work. To resume, open History and choose Saved drafts. To apply an edit to the task, use Save in the section you edited.

When you restore a draft, reselect any file marked “Reselection required.” If the file is marked as reusable, continue with the existing upload.

If a draft conflicts with server content, review the differences, then explicitly restore or delete the old draft. When editing the same task in multiple pages, close older pages first.

title: Question and material upload
intro: Only a question source is required; you can upload the other materials or have SmarTAI prepare them.

sections.title: What goes in each of the four material categories
sections.body:
Upload one question file or select one from the course library. Include the full question, conditions and figures.

  • Reference answers may contain just the final answers. Check the solution steps during question review.
  • Grading criteria can come from a file or the course library. You can also type the scoring rules.
  • Programming test cases should give the input and expected output for each case. You can upload paired examples as JSON or CSV.

Select up to one source per category. Each new file can be up to 5 MiB, with up to 400,000 characters of extracted text. All four categories accept documents and still images. See Upload formats at a glance.

For images or scanned PDFs that need recognition, choose an OCR or vision-capable model. For grading criteria or test cases, also select “Enable visual OCR for this material.”

details.title: Add missing materials or save a source for later
details.body: With a generative model, you can start with just the questions and review the generated reference answers and grading criteria. With Baidu OCR alone, fill gaps during review or select a generative model. Select “Also save to course library” to reuse a document or still image. Library images use the recognition model.

sections.title: Narrow the recognition scope
sections.body:
“Already organized by question” suits assignment files with clear question numbers; “Extract from source text” suits textbooks and long documents. Specify page numbers, target question numbers, and additional instructions as needed to avoid adding all exercises from an entire textbook.

  • Count from the first page of the PDF. For example, 3-5, 8 selects pages 3 through 5 and page 8 of the file.
  • Question numbers can be 1.1.5, 1.2.3; a range within the same section can be written as 1.1.5-1.1.7.
  • Put instructions such as “Chapter 3 exercises; retain figures and tables” in additional instructions.

When describing grading criteria in natural language, choose “By question” or “Overall rules.” For question-specific descriptions, clearly state question numbers. Overall rules are organized into scoring steps using each question’s reference answer.

sections.title: Set maximum scores and generation language
sections.body:
Under “Set question maximum scores,” enter a uniform value, or enable “Different maximum scores per question” and describe the scores by question number. For example: “Questions 1–3: 5 points each; Question 4: 15 points.”

Questions without an explicit setting or a matching rule temporarily default to 10 points, with a reminder to check. After recognition, verify maximum scores in question details. Model grading uses each question’s saved maximum score.

Choose Chinese or English as the generation language, select a “Question recognition model,” then click “Recognize and prepare question materials.” The chosen language is retained for material generation, supplementary generation, and retries. Changing the interface language does not overwrite it.

sections.title: Track progress or take over midway
sections.body:
The progress page shows completion counts, percentages, and recognition activity. Waiting for capacity, waiting for a response, and retrying are shown separately. You can return to the workspace and check again later.

After a pause or failure, follow the prompts to retry or “Continue manually.” Manual takeover opens the original question matrix and retains recognized content and available originals. If the total number of questions is unknown, set the complete count first, then fill in each question.

If pages are unread or questions are missing, retry those pages or use the original file to add the missing questions. If the previous request may have been billed, check the charge notice before retrying.

details.title: What manual review retains
details.body: Saved results open directly without calling a model or using model quota. Existing fields are retained; complete missing fields in the original review matrix.

title: Review questions and complete materials
intro: Check questions and point values first, then confirm reference answers, grading criteria, and programming test materials.

sections.title: Find questions that need attention in the matrix
sections.body:
The question overview shows preparation status by question, with search, filters, and detail views. Open red “Action required” items first, then yellow recommendations. You can add question rows or remove rows that do not belong to this assignment from the current scope.

In details, compare question text, reference answers, grading criteria, and test materials against the originals. Edit and save each content area separately. Confirmation and question-navigation buttons support continuous question-by-question review.

Material text may be locked at later stages, while browsing and review confirmation remain available. To make changes, first use the task’s back or redo action.

Use the original-file preview to compare images or to zoom and jump to a page in a PDF. For a text file such as TXT, read the recognized text in question details.

sections.title: Check maximum scores and grading criteria together
sections.body:
You can edit “Maximum score and grading criteria for this question” together. Maximum scores must be positive numbers from 0.01–10000, with no more than two decimal places. If criteria explicitly assign points to subquestions, those subquestions still belong to the same main question, and their points must add up to its maximum score.

If no absolute component scores are specified, use percentages or free-text grading criteria, for example, “Derivation: 60%; conclusion: 40%.” Generated process-based scoring is organized by the corresponding steps. For objective questions, check the applicable result-based rules.

Fill in and save any missing question text or grading criteria. If the points for the parts do not add up to the maximum, check the original question, correct the values and save.

sections.title: Three ways to add materials
sections.body:
• Edit a single item. Open the question, make your change and save.
  • Bulk import materials. Select reference answers, grading criteria or test cases, then choose one file or one library item. All targets accept documents and still images. Selecting “Test cases” also enables JSON and CSV. New files can be up to 5 MiB, with up to 400,000 characters of extracted text.
  • Complete missing items. Review the list, clear anything you want to skip and confirm generation.

After importing, check the matched question numbers and select “Apply confirmed matches.” Select overwrite if you want to replace existing content.

details.title: Import scans or save a copy to the library
details.body: Enable visual OCR when importing an image or scanned PDF as grading criteria or test cases. JSON and CSV are used for the current import. To reuse a document or still image later, select “Also save to course library.”

sections.title: Extra checks for programming questions
sections.body:
Check the sample correct code, execution mode, each test input, expected output, and explanation. Function-mode and standard-input-mode materials use their corresponding structures. Expand the cases and check each input against its expected output.

An empty string can be a valid test value and is different from a missing field. The page distinguishes “Public examples” from “Hidden tests.” Click “Edit” to change titles, inputs, expected outputs, explanations, and public/hidden types, or to add and remove cases. Then click “Save test cases.” Check source labels to distinguish generated content, uploaded content, and teacher confirmation status.

title: Upload and review student submissions
intro: Match each submission to the right student, then confirm the recognized content for every question.

sections.title: Organize and upload submissions
sections.body:
Collect one self-contained source file per student. Python supports top-level functions and standard input/output programs. C11 and C++17 support complete programs that read standard input and write standard output. In a class ZIP, files with the same name can be placed in separate student folders. For handwritten Python, upload a clear image or scanned PDF, select a vision-capable model and check the transcribed indentation and symbols. If a program depends on other source files, combine it into one independently runnable file before submission.

Written assignments. Collect one document or still image per student, for example 00123_Alex.pdf. Upload an individual submission or a class archive. Choose an OCR or vision-capable model for images and scanned PDFs.

Choose one file at a time, up to 100 MiB. Individual images can be up to 10 MiB. Choose how to match students, then select Start Submission Recognition.

details.title: Class archive formats and limits
details.body:
You can keep the folder structure inside the archive. Archives inside another archive are not supported.

Accepted formats are ZIP, RAR, 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ, TGZ, TAR.BZ2 and TBZ2. Include up to 500 files, up to 5 MiB each and 100 MiB total when unpacked. Split a class-wide PDF by student before uploading.

details.title: Uploading again after recognition
details.body: A new upload replaces the current recognized submissions and requires new grading results. Create a new task for a different assignment.

sections.title: Choose an identity-matching method
sections.body:
• Match by filename. Include the student ID and name in each filename, then check the matches.
  • Import a roster. Choose CSV (commas), TSV (tabs) or TXT (either delimiter). Put the headers on the first line. Student ID is required and name is optional.
  • Correct manually. Check each student’s identity after recognition.

Example CSV roster:

student_id,name
00123,Alex
00124,Sam

details.title: Roster encoding and alternative headers
details.body: UTF-8 is recommended. UTF-8 with BOM and GBK are also accepted. The ID header may be student_id, stu_id or 学号. For names, use student_name, stu_name, name or 姓名. Use a single column for each field you include. Leading zeros in IDs are preserved.

sections.title: Check identities, answers, and originals
sections.body:
In the student submission matrix, check student rows and question statuses. Open student details and compare identities and answers against the originals. You can add or remove student rows in the current scope. During manual takeover, if the student count is unknown, enter the full count first.

Resolve name, student ID, and identity conflicts, as well as missing expected answer records. If content is correct but still marked as awaiting confirmation, retain its value and explicitly confirm it.

If an answer appears blank, open the student’s original file. If it contains an answer, retry recognition or enter the answer manually and save it. If the student left it blank, confirm the blank response.

sections.title: When recognition is incomplete
sections.body: Open the recognition results and check which files need attention. Resume a paused job, retry unread pages with the original file, or continue manually to fill gaps. Resolve the red items before opening grading setup.

details.title: Empty files and archive errors
details.body: If a student file is empty, replace it in the archive and upload again. If the extraction service is temporarily unavailable, retry the saved file later. RAR needs a server-side extraction tool; ZIP is a convenient choice for a class set.

details.title: What manual review retains
details.body: Saved results open directly without calling a model or using model quota. Existing fields are retained; complete missing fields in the original review matrix.

title: Configure and run grading
intro: Choose models, a scoring method, and a feedback style for this task, then check the summary and begin grading.

sections.title: Choose models and score aggregation
sections.body:
Select at least one enabled model. Selections here apply only to this task and do not change global enabled states in “Models & BYOK.”

  • Single-model grading: calls only the selected model.
  • Weighted average: by default, combines valid scores using confidence weights. You can change this to custom positive ratios, such as 1:2.
  • Combined review: the lead model synthesizes comments. Scores still use the configured weights, and additional model calls are required.

Failed experts are excluded from score aggregation, and the remaining weights are renormalized. If no valid confidence values are available, an equally weighted average is used. Final AI scores retain one decimal place.

sections.title: Scoring, feedback, and materials
sections.body:
Choose grading strictness and whether to allow partial credit. Advanced settings let you adjust comment tone, length, language, improvement suggestions, the number of samples for a single model, and grading instructions.

To use textbooks or lecture notes, select them from the course library or upload documents and still images for this task. Documents can be up to 64 MiB each and images up to 10 MiB each. Select up to 20 files in total. Images uploaded here use the default vision/OCR model. To choose a model, upload in the course library first, then attach the material.

Multiple sampling applies only to a single model configured with your own credentials and increases calls. When multiple models are selected, each runs once. If platform-shared models are available, they must be used alone with a fixed single sample.

sections.title: Saving starts an automatic countdown
sections.body:
Click “Save and view grading summary” and check question and student counts, grading criteria, reference answers, expert selection, and scoring strategy. Once checks pass, a countdown starts automatically. You can also click “Start grading now.” To make changes, click “Back to grading settings.”

If red issues remain, the summary provides links to questions, submissions, or model settings. Resolve them, then save the settings again. After a pause or failure, saving again starts a new summary flow even if the configuration is unchanged.

sections.title: Progress, pause, and resume
sections.body:
The progress page shows each model’s completed work, waiting for capacity, waiting for responses, and retries, along with saved AI work and aggregated student-question results. Expand the activity log for details. You can leave the page while processing continues in the background.

When grading is paused, resume the remaining work or choose the manual option to complete missing scores and comments in review. Each model’s progress counts its own completed items. The aggregated count shows how many answers have a combined score.

Resuming reuses compatible saved results. Recognizing all materials again or regrading the entire batch reruns a broader scope. Read the button labels and prompts carefully before starting.

title: Review scores and regrade
intro: Locate issues in the class matrix, then compare answers, grading evidence, and expert feedback to decide final scores.

sections.title: Resolve red items first, then check yellow
sections.body:
Red “Action required” items show the reason. For a missing or out-of-range score, open the item, check the answer, enter a score from zero to the question maximum and save. When a programming question asks for your grading decision, review the test results and either confirm the proposed score or edit and save your own.

Yellow “Suggested review” items can indicate low confidence, disagreement between models, or a result from only some models. You can review them now or continue to results.

details.title: When are low confidence and score disagreement flagged?
details.body: A confidence below 0.60 flags a model’s score for review. Disagreement is flagged when at least two models have valid scores and the population standard deviation of those scores exceeds 15% of the question’s maximum score.

sections.title: Review and confirm each question
sections.body:
In the review table, select the status icon where the student’s row meets the question’s column. Compare the original answer with the grading criteria and model comments. To change the score or feedback, edit the teacher’s final result and save.

Use the confirmation button to record that you have reviewed the answer. Use the previous and next question controls to review more answers from the same student.

To add or remove questions or students, return to question preparation or submission review.

sections.title: Retry failed items or regrade the entire batch
sections.body:
• Retry failed items only: completes unfinished model work while retaining saved teacher score changes and annotations.
  • Regrade entire batch: opens regrading settings and a summary, then explicitly starts a new round. It reruns grading even when inputs are unchanged.

After reviewing the new round, open “Reports & downloads” to generate a new version. Earlier reports retain the scores and comments they contained when generated.

title: Results analysis and reports
intro: Open the results page for a class overview. Choose Question analysis to find lower-scoring questions, or Student analysis to see one student’s performance.

sections.title: Overview and question analysis
sections.body:
The overview shows student and question counts, the class average score percentage, pass rate, score distribution, and weaker questions. Click “Question analysis” to examine performance by question, then open details for question materials, student answers, and scores.

Search, filters, and sorting help locate low-scoring questions or items needing review. To change scores, select “Review History.” Statistics and charts update after saving.

sections.title: Student analysis
sections.body:
The student table shows total scores, score percentages, question scores, and review indicators, with column sorting and filtering. Open a student’s details for individual performance by question; click a specific score to locate that question.

Enter clear conditions in Ask, for example, “Filter students with score percentages below 60%, sorted from lowest to highest.” Check the returned filter conditions and clear them when needed to restore the whole class.

For duplicate or exact names, supply identity details when prompted for clarification. Confidence indicates how certain the model was about this score.

sections.title: Ask and visual analysis
sections.body:
Open “Visual analysis.” Choose an example above the Ask SmarTAI box or type a question such as “Compare average scores as a percentage of the maximum for each question.” Select “Ask SmarTAI” to generate a chart, using model quota as needed.

Ask can request charts, filters, and sorting in one request. Charts and the main table can use different scopes, such as a whole-class chart alongside a list of low-scoring students. Check the sample and scope labeled on each chart.

Default charts include score-percentage distribution, pass/fail composition, per-question score percentages and review counts, scatter plots, and student × question heatmaps. Use the page controls to export charts or print.

Use the PNG button on the chart to keep or share a copy. Saving a custom chart for this visit makes it available during the current browsing session.

sections.title: Generate and download reports
sections.body:
1. Open “Reports and downloads” and confirm that review requirements are satisfied.
  2. Select “Generate files” to create the current version.
  3. Select the download button beside a file, or choose “Download all ZIP.”
  4. After changing scores or regrading, regenerate reports and check the version number and generation time.
  • Grade sheet CSV: final scores, total score percentages, and scores by question.
  • Learning report Markdown: factual summaries for the class, questions, and students.
  • Publication-ready reference answers in Markdown / LaTeX: question text, grading criteria, and reference answers.
  • Official results JSON: a complete results snapshot.

To see scores as they were at an earlier date, download that version. Deleting a report version removes its files and preserves the grades and review records.

title: Account settings and common issues
intro: Adjust display preferences and check storage usage. When something blocks progress, start with the reason shown on the page.

sections.title: Interface and storage
sections.body:
Open the username menu in the upper-right corner → “Account settings” to view your username, email, and role. Choose Chinese or English, and light, dark, or system appearance. Interface preferences are saved only in the current browser.

Task original-file storage includes original questions, submission packages, and original student answers; library storage is counted separately. When originals are cleaned up under retention rules, structured results, analysis, and long-term library content remain, but original-file previews may no longer be available.

You can also manage local drafts in account settings. Before deleting, confirm that you no longer need the content that has not been formally saved.

Task originals and course library materials have separate storage limits, each 512 MB by default. This page shows how much you have used and the current limit for each.

sections.title: A button is unavailable
sections.body:
Click or read the reason near the button. Common causes include a missing question file, no available model, a roster not yet uploaded, files being checked, the material limit being reached, or unresolved red required items. Follow the prompt to resolve the issue before continuing.

If an item remains under “Action required,” open its message to see which question, answer or score needs attention. Correct it and save. For a genuinely blank answer or a programming score awaiting your decision, follow the confirmation prompt for that item.

sections.title: Model failures, page conflicts, or missing files
sections.body:
• Key or permission issues: check the provider, API key, and model ID in “Models & BYOK.”
  • Model or endpoint not found: check both the Model ID and Base URL.
  • Timeout or rate limiting: retain current files and configuration, then retry later or choose another available model.
  • Content changed on another page: reload the latest state, check retained edits, then save.
  • Only a filename remains: select the file again. Original reusable: continue directly. Check failed: retry the check first.

Prefer “Resume” or “Retry failed items only” to complete remaining work. Choose “Recognize all again” or “Regrade entire batch” only when a complete rerun is needed.

title: Configure models in SmarTAI
intro: Add your own API Key, save the configuration, and test text and image capabilities as needed.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.body:
SmarTAI supports models from different providers using your own API Key. Add a configuration by following the steps below.

No local proxy setup required: Model requests are sent by SmarTAI's platform servers. You do not need to enable or switch a local VPN/network proxy for different providers. Actual requests must still meet the provider's account permission, supported-region, and API connectivity requirements.

Guide version: November 2026. Models, free quotas, application procedures, and request limits may change. Refer to the provider's official documentation and your own account console for current information.

sections.title: Open “Models & BYOK”
sections.body:
Open your username menu at the top right and select “Models & BYOK.” You can also select the enabled-model count at the top, then “Manage Models & BYOK.”

On the configuration page, select “Add configuration” at the top right.

sections.title: Complete and save the configuration
sections.body:
First, find your provider in Section 2, follow the steps to obtain a key, and then enter the following details.

FieldWhat to enter
ProviderSelect the relevant provider.
Configuration nameOptional, for example, “Assignment grading” or “Image recognition.” If left blank, the model name is used by default.
Model nameCopy the provider's Model ID. This is the name used to call the model, such as gemini-3.5-flash-lite, as shown in the provider’s documentation.
API keyPaste the complete key and remove any leading or trailing spaces.
API Base URLEnter the API base address. You can copy it directly from the relevant provider section.
API protocolWhen using the provider's official API, keep this set to Follow provider.
RPMThe number of requests allowed per minute. Enter the value supplied by the provider; if you are unsure, leave it blank or enter 0.
ConcurrencyAdjusted automatically; no entry is needed.

Click Save configuration and confirm that the configuration is Enabled. For configurations you use often, choose Set as default. To use multiple models, add a separate configuration for each.

Keep your API key private like a password. Cover it before sharing a screenshot. SmarTAI hides the full key after saving. When editing a configuration, leave the key field blank to keep the existing key.

Costs and limits. Open Billing in the provider console to check your balance, free credits and expiry dates. Open Limits to check request limits. Both input and output count toward token usage. Charges after free credits run out depend on your billing settings. Leaving RPM blank or entering 0 enables automatic pacing within your provider account’s limits.

sections.title: Test API connectivity
sections.body:
After saving, you can test the configuration as needed:

TestActionWhat it checks
Text testClick Verify (optional) → Run connectivity check.Whether the key, model name, and API address work correctly.
Image testClick Verify vision capability → Run image test.Whether the current model configuration can read images correctly.

Confirming a test sends one request to the provider, uses quota and may incur a charge. To test later, choose Cancel.

The image test uses a built-in sample. If the result is inconclusive, open the reason and check the model’s image support and your account quota.

After the test passes, check the recognized text against the original file in your assignment.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.body:
Message or symptomWhat to do
Invalid key, incorrect format, or insufficient permissionsCopy the API Key again and check that you selected the correct provider, region, and key type.
Model or endpoint not foundCheck the Model ID and API Base URL, and confirm that the model has been enabled for your account.
Rate limit reached or insufficient quotaCheck the provider's balance, promotional-credit expiry date, and request limits. For per-minute rate limits, retry later; for daily quotas, wait for the provider to reset them.
Text test passes but image test failsConfirm that the selected model supports images, then check the quota and error message.
Connection failure or request timeoutRetry later and check the API address, the provider's service status, and supported regions. If the issue persists, contact the platform administrator.

You can select different models for question recognition, answer recognition, and grading. Images, scans, and handwritten answers require an image-capable model. Baidu OCR handles recognition only; subsequent grading still requires a large language model.

title: Providers and API access
intro: Find a provider and review the application steps, configuration details, and free or trial quotas.

sections.title: Choose a provider
sections.body:
Select your provider to find the steps for getting a key and the values to enter in SmarTAI.

Network access note: In some network environments, accessing the official websites and API consoles for Google Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic Claude may require a VPN/network proxy. When applying for and using an API, also comply with the provider's supported-region requirements.

Once the model is configured, SmarTAI sends the requests from its servers.

  • Google Gemini / Gemma
  • OpenAI
  • Anthropic Claude
  • DeepSeek
  • Zhipu BigModel / GLM
  • Kimi / Moonshot
  • Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / Qwen
  • Baidu Document Parsing Unlimited-OCR
  • Tencent Hunyuan / TokenHub
  • ByteDance Doubao / Volcano Ark
  • MiniMax

The configuration examples below use the providers' official APIs. For school-provided or other relay APIs, see Section 3.

title: Google Gemini / Gemma
intro: Access and configuration · Google Gemini / Gemma

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body:
Free quota: The models below offer an API free tier. Check the current project in AI Studio for specific request and token limits. Multiple keys in the same project share the quota.

Google's free tier has different data-handling rules from the paid tier, and content may be used to improve products. Read the provider's rules before use, and avoid uploading personal information without authorization. See the official explanation.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Open Google AI Studio and sign in with your Google account.
  2. Go to Dashboard → API Keys and click Create API key.
  3. Select a project. If this is your first time, follow the page instructions to create a project, then copy the generated key.
  4. In Rate Limit, select the same project, check the target model's RPM, and enter it in SmarTAI.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderGoogle Gemini
Model namegemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.8-flash, gemma-4-31b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it. Choose any one; all support text and images.
API keyThe Google AI Studio key you just copied.
API Base URLhttps://generativelanguage.googleapis.com
API protocolFollow provider (Gemini generateContent).

Model differences: gemini-3.5-flash-lite focuses on speed and low cost; gemini-3.8-flash focuses on overall capabilities; gemma-4-31b-it and gemma-4-26b-a4b-it are open-weight models, with the latter using a more efficient MoE architecture. All the models above support text and image input.

Gemma also uses the Google Gemini entry here. Before use, check the Supported regions.

Official references: API key instructions · Gemini models · Gemma models · Pricing and free tier.

title: OpenAI
intro: Access and configuration · OpenAI

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body:
Free quota: The models below have no general API free tier; valid API credits can offset usage charges. Eligible ChatGPT Pro subscriptions with access to this benefit can claim $100 / $200 / $500 in monthly API credits, matching the subscription tier. Business credits depend on paid seats; see the official guide and availability details.

Claim and use: Your paid subscription must be at least 7 days old. Use the same email for ChatGPT and API accounts, and own both the subscription (or Business workspace) and receiving API organization. Claim and link that organization in OpenAI Platform Billing, then use its project API key in SmarTAI. No API payment method is required while valid free credits remain. The first grant is prorated; credits expire at the billing cycle's end without rolling over. Renewal grants are automatic while the benefit remains available and your subscription stays eligible.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Sign in to OpenAI Platform and confirm the organization and project you want to use.
  2. Open API keys and click Create new secret key.
  3. You can enter SmarTAI as the name. Copy the key immediately after creating it.
  4. In the console, open Billing to check your available balance or credits, and open Limits to check the target model's RPM.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderOpenAI
Model namegpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra. Choose any one; all support text and images.
API keyThe OpenAI API key you just created.
API Base URLhttps://api.openai.com/v1
API protocolFollow provider (OpenAI Chat Completions).

Model differences: gpt-6-luna focuses on speed and low cost; gpt-6.1-sol balances capabilities and cost; gpt-6-astra is designed for more complex reasoning tasks. All three support text and image input.

Official references: Quickstart · Model list · API pricing · Supported regions.

title: Anthropic Claude
intro: Access and configuration · Anthropic Claude

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body:
Free quota: New users may receive a small API trial credit; check Billing in the Console for the actual amount and expiry date. Eligible Max / Team subscribers can claim included API credits, and research projects can apply for dedicated credits. Standard API usage is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis.

Max / Team users can open Billing → API credits on the Claude website to link a Console organization and claim credits. New subscriptions must be at least 7 days old. Credits expire at the end of the billing period and do not roll over. For eligibility and amounts, see API credits for subscribers.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Sign in to Claude Platform.
  2. Go to Settings → API Keys and click Create key.
  3. Select a workspace. You can use the name SmarTAI, then copy the key after creating it.
  4. In Billing, check your valid credits, and in Usage → Limits, check your current RPM.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderClaude (Anthropic)
Model nameclaude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5. Choose any one; all support text and images.
API keyThe Claude API key you just created.
API Base URLhttps://api.anthropic.com
API protocolFollow provider (Anthropic Messages).

Model differences: claude-haiku-5-5 focuses on speed and low cost; claude-sonnet-5-5 balances speed and capabilities; claude-opus-5-5 is designed for more complex tasks. All three support text and image input.

Official references: API introduction · Model list · Pricing and trials · Apply for research credits · Supported regions.

title: DeepSeek
intro: Access and configuration · DeepSeek

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body: Free credits. API use is billed by usage. Existing promotional credit is applied first. Check your balance on the API platform for credits available to your account.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Sign in to DeepSeek Platform.
  2. Open API keys, then create and copy a key.
  3. In Balance, check your purchased balance, promotional balance, and expiry dates. Top up as needed if your balance is insufficient.
  4. Return to SmarTAI, select DeepSeek, enter the details below, and save.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderDeepSeek
Model namedeepseek-flash: text and images; deepseek-v4-pro: text. Choose either one.
API keyThe DeepSeek key you just created.
API Base URLhttps://api.deepseek.com/v1

Model differences: deepseek-flash supports text and image input and is suitable for general grading and image recognition; deepseek-v4-pro supports text input only and can be used for text-only grading and review. For image recognition, select deepseek-flash.

RPM measures requests per minute. If the provider lists only a concurrency limit, leave RPM blank.

Official references: Your first API call · Models and pricing · Rate-limit details.

title: Zhipu BigModel / GLM
intro: Access and configuration · Zhipu BigModel / GLM

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body: Free quota: glm-4.7-flash and glm-4.6v-flash are currently free; glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash use pay-as-you-go billing. After receiving a new-user resource package, check which models it covers and when it expires.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Register or sign in to BigModel.
  2. Open API Keys, select Standard API Key, and create a key.
  3. Copy the standard API key you just created.
  4. Check resource packages, usage, and limits in the console, then return to SmarTAI to enter the details.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderZhipu
Model nameText: glm-4.7-flash, glm-5.3; text/images: glm-4.6v-flash, glm-5.3-flash. Choose any one.
API keyThe newly created Standard API Key.
API Base URLhttps://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4
API protocolFollow provider (OpenAI Chat Completions).

Model differences: glm-4.7-flash is a free text model; glm-4.6v-flash is a free vision model. glm-5.3 is designed for complex text tasks, and glm-5.3-flash supports text and image input. Standard API usage for the latter two is normally billed on a pay-as-you-go basis.

The configuration above is for the mainland China BigModel platform. If you have an overseas Z.ai account, use that site's Key and address, https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4.

Official references: Quickstart · Model list · Pricing · Key types.

title: Kimi / Moonshot
intro: Access and configuration · Kimi / Moonshot

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body: Free quota: New users registering with a mainland China mobile number can receive an RMB 15 API voucher after completing real-name verification. It is valid for 3 months. Usage of Kimi K3 is charged to the account balance. For eligible models, the voucher is used first, then the account balance.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Register or sign in to Kimi API Platform.
  2. Complete real-name verification in the user center and check whether the new-user voucher has been credited.
  3. Go to API Keys, then create and copy a key.
  4. Check billing details for the models covered by the voucher and its expiry date, and check the rate-limits page for RPM.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderKimi (Moonshot)
Model namekimi-k3 supports text and images.
API keyYour API key from the Kimi Platform.
API Base URLhttps://api.moonshot.cn/v1
API protocolFollow provider (OpenAI Chat Completions).

Model notes: kimi-k3 is designed for complex reasoning and long-text tasks. It supports text and image input but is not covered by this new-user voucher.

Kimi web subscriptions, Kimi Code, and API balances are separate. The overseas platform platform.kimi.ai uses https://api.moonshot.ai/v1, and its accounts, keys, and balances are independent of the mainland China site.

Official references: Free benefits for new users · Model list · Rate limits · FAQ.

title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / Qwen
intro: Access and configuration · Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / Qwen

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body: Free quota: Eligible new users in China (Beijing), China North 2, receive a quota of 1 million tokens for each of the two models below, usually valid for 90 days. If you only want to use the free quota, enable Stop when free quota is exhausted.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Sign in to Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, select the region China North 2 (Beijing), and follow the prompts to activate the service.
  2. Open API Key page and click Create API Key. For personal use, you can select the primary account and default workspace, and create the key with the page's default permissions.
  3. Copy the key. On the Free quota page, search for the target model, check the remaining quota and expiry date, and enable Stop when exhausted as needed.
  4. Return to SmarTAI, select Qwen, and enter the details below. Paste the standard Beijing-region key into the API key field.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:
FieldValue
ProviderQwen (Tongyi Qianwen)
Model nameqwen3.8-max or qwen3.8-flash. Both support text and images.
API keyA standard API key created in the Beijing region.
API Base URLhttps://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
API protocolFollow provider (OpenAI Chat Completions).

Model differences: qwen3.8-max is the flagship model, focusing on complex reasoning and multimodal understanding; qwen3.8-flash focuses on speed and low cost. Both support text and image input. Check your own console for the new-user free quota.

These two models use dynamic rate limiting. If the page does not provide an RPM value, leave it blank or enter 0. If you select a different region, use the key and address for that region as well.

Official references: Obtain a key · New-user quota rules · Models and pricing · Rate-limit details.

title: Baidu Document Parsing Unlimited-OCR
intro: Access and configuration · Baidu Document Parsing Unlimited-OCR

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body:
Free quota: The current limited-time free quota is 200 pages for individually verified accounts and 1000 pages for enterprise-verified accounts. Check the OCR console for your remaining pages and expiry date.

When to use it. Select Unlimited-OCR to extract text and structure from images, PDFs and other documents. In grading settings, select a grading model to score the assignments.

sections.title: Obtain and save credentials
sections.body:
1. Register or sign in to Baidu AI Cloud and complete individual or enterprise real-name verification.
  2. Go to OCR console, activate Document Parsing (Unlimited-OCR), and check the resource list for your free page quota.
  3. Go to Application list → Create application and select the permissions for the document parsing API.
  4. In the application list, copy the application's API Key and Secret Key.
  5. Return to “Models & BYOK” in SmarTAI and find Baidu Document Parsing (Unlimited-OCR). Enter the API Key and Secret Key into their respective fields, then click “Save credentials.”

After saving, click Verify API Key / Secret Key to check the credentials. For actual recognition, select Baidu OCR in the task. Credential verification does not submit a file. Actual OCR calls consume pages, and failed calls may also consume free resources.

Official references: Beginner's guide · Unlimited-OCR overview · Free resource rules.

title: Tencent Hunyuan / TokenHub
intro: Access and configuration · Tencent Hunyuan / TokenHub

sections.title: Quotas and usage notes
sections.body: Free quota: The current new-user promotion ends on 2026-12-31. Language and multimodal-understanding models offer a trial quota of 1 million tokens, valid for 1 year after claiming it. Check “Activation management” for eligible models, remaining quota, and expiry dates. If postpaid billing is not enabled, calls stop when the free quota is exhausted.

sections.title: Obtain an API key
sections.body:
1. Sign in to Tencent Cloud TokenHub and complete real-name verification.
  2. Go to Model marketplace → Free trial for new users, select the models you want to use, and click Claim now.
  3. Go to API Key management, select the Guangzhou region and click Create API Key.
  4. You can enter SmarTAI as the name. Under “Scope,” select the models you want to use, confirm, and copy the full key.

sections.title: Enter the details in SmarTAI
sections.body:

API Base URLhttps://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1
API protocolFollow provider (OpenAI Chat Completions).

Model differences: hy3 is a general-purpose text reasoning model; hy-vision-2.0-instruct is a vision-understanding model that supports image content recognition, OCR, and chart understanding. Choose the latter when you need image recognition.

Official references: Getting started · Model list · Image understanding · New-user quota rules.

intro: Access and configuration · ByteDance Doubao / Volcano Ark

  2. In Activation management, find the model you want to use, follow the prompts to activate its free trial, and enable Worry-free trial mode as needed.
  3. Go to API Key management and click Create API Key. For personal use, you can keep the default project workspace.
  4. You can enter SmarTAI as the name, then view and copy the key from the list after creating it.

title: School-provided and other relay APIs
intro: When using an API provided by a school or institution, follow its configuration details and limits.

sections.title: Obtain and enter the configuration
sections.body:
If you use an API provided by a school, institution, or another relay provider, first obtain the API Key, API Base URL, Model ID, and API protocol from them, then enter the details according to their documentation.

FieldHow to enter it
ProviderSelect the provider specified in the relay provider's documentation.
API keyEnter the key supplied by the relay provider.
API Base URLCopy the base URL supplied by your school or relay provider.
Model nameEnter the relay provider's Model ID. The same model may have different names on different relay services.
API protocol, RPMUse the values in the relay provider's documentation or those supplied by the administrator.

For example, if your school gives you https://example.edu/v1, paste that exact address into API Base URL.

After saving, check the configuration using the text and image tests. If you encounter problems with the key, balance, model name, API address, or connection, contact the relay provider or school administrator first and provide the error message. Follow their documentation for the specific configuration procedure.
